items.title: A HOME WORTH FIGHTING FOR
items.body:
In Cinema – Maysles Documentary Center
Wednesday, September 16th, 2026 at 7PM

NYCHA: Promise and Peril series

TICKETS

General Admission: $15 / Reduced: $7

A HOME WORTH FIGHTING FOR:
The Push to Stop the Demolition of Public Housing in Chelsea

Natasha Florentino, 2025, 40 min

Through the eyes of longtime residents fighting to save their homes, A Home Worth Fighting For, exposes a flawed political process that prioritizes private developers over the preservation of public housing and dismisses calls for transparency. While pitched as resident driven, this proposed demolition clearly aims to clear valuable land in Chelsea to make way for market rate development on public land. Determined to defend their community, residents organize to resist a profit-driven plan aimed at privatizing public housing.

Followed by:

FOR THOSE WHO LIVED THERE

Shawn Antoine II, 2024, 7 min

Amidst the gentrified remnants of Chicago's Cabrini Green, FOR THOSE WHO LIVED THERE captures the haunting displacement of Black legacies and the emergence of migrant narratives.

Post screening conversation with NATASHA FLORENTINO, director of A HOME WORTH FIGHTING FOR, Shawn Antoine II, director of FOR THOSE WHO LIVED THERE, and Renee Keitt, the resident council president of Elliott-Chelsea houses

Post screening conversation with Natasha Florentino, Shawn Antoine II and Renee Keitt

LEGACY SPIRIT OF THE BLACK PANTHERS

Jermaine Taishi Thomas, 30 min

LEGACY SPIRIT provides an historical overview of the Kansas City Chapter of the Black Panther Party founded by Pete O'Neal (currently in exile in Tanzania). Interviews with past members and file footage offer insight into the original intent of the organization; police brutality; provide food and educational services to members of the community as well as health screenings, all components of the model of self help. The story is told through the eyes of members from The Kansas City Chapter. The media paints a picture of a radical organization but they were an organization of service. The film also features an interview from Pete O’Neal.

items.title: An Afternoon with ASHANTI ALSTON in Conversation with Joy James (FREE Event)
items.body:
In Cinema – Maysles Documentary Center
Sunday, September 27th, 2026 at 4:30PM

Co-presented with AK Press

FREE - Rsvp

FREE – DONATIONS WELCOME

An Afternoon With
ASHANTI OMOWALI ALSTON

What does it mean to remain committed to liberation while allowing your ideas about liberation to change?

Join Maysles Documentary Center for an afternoon with Ashanti Omowali Alston, writer, organizer, former member of the Black Panther Party and Black Liberation Army, and an important voice in the development of Black anarchist thought.

Alston’s political journey stretches from the Black freedom struggles of the 1960s and ’70s through political imprisonment, anarchism, abolition, solidarity with the Zapatistas, and decades of organizing and reflection. Throughout, he has returned to a basic question: how can movements learn from their histories without becoming trapped by them?

The conversation marks the publication of Anarchist Panther: The Selected Writings of Ashanti O. Alston, a new collection from AK Press bringing together Alston’s writing and speeches on the Panthers, political prisoners, feminism, Black anarchism, the Zapatistas, and the possibilities of revolutionary transformation.

Following our 2 PM screening of FULL MANTIS, a portrait of visionary percussionist Milford Graves, we turn from musical improvisation to political improvisation: the ability to listen, adapt, question inherited forms, and create something new.

This is not simply a conversation about the movements of the past. It is an invitation to think together about what those histories might offer us now.

How do we carry a revolutionary tradition forward while remaining free enough to transform it?

JOY JAMES is Ebenezer Fitch Professor of Humanities at Williams College. She is the author of Resisting State Violence; Shadowboxing: Representations of Black Feminist Politics, Transcending the Talented Tenth and Seeking the Beloved Community.

This talk is co-sponsored by AK PRESS.

items.title: MILFORD GRAVES:  FULL MANTIS
items.body:
In Cinema – Maysles Documentary Center
Sunday, September 27th, 2026 at 2PM

Co-presented with AK Press

TICKETS

General Admission: $15 / Reduced: $7

MILFORD GRAVES: FULL MANTIS
The Revolutionary as Improviser

Jake Meginsky, Neil Young, 2018, 92 min.

2:00 PM — FULL MANTIS

4:30 PM — An Afternoon with Ashanti Alston: Conversation with Joy James + Q&A

Join us for an afternoon exploring improvisation as a practice of freedom, beginning with FULL MANTIS, an intimate portrait of percussionist and visionary Milford Graves.

Graves approached improvisation as more than a musical technique. It was a way of thinking through the body, discipline, healing, self-determination, and the creation of new forms. His restless experimentation provides a provocative starting point for a conversation between Joy James and Ashanti Alston. 

Alston’s journey from the Black Panther Party and Black Liberation Army to anarchism and abolition has similarly involved questioning inherited structures and imagining new ones.

Following the film, Alston joins us at 4:30 PM for a conversation about Black liberation, revolutionary practice, and ideas explored in his writing, including Anarchist Panther: Selected Writings

Come for the film, stay for the conversation—or join us at 4:30 PM for Ashanti Alston. Film admission includes priority seating for the Ashanti Alston conversation.

items.body:
In Cinema – Maysles Documentary Center

BLACK PANTHER PARTY FILM FESTIVAL Series

TICKETS

General Admission: $15 / Reduced: $7


A PANTHER IN AFRICA

Aaron Matthews, 2004, 71 min.

Pete O'Neal, a young Black Panther in Kansas City, Missouri, was arrested for transporting a gun across state lines in October 1969. O'Neal evaded the charge a year later and moved to Tanzania. For over 30 years he has lived there, an American exile from a time when activists felt themselves to be warring with the U.S. government. Today, O’Neal, a community organizer, encounters very different challenges living between cultural and political spheres – African and American – navigating a radical past and an uncertain future.

Post-screening discussion with filmmaker Aaron Matthews and one of the main characters in the documentary, Charlotte O’Neal!

Set to an original score by jazz pianist Lafayette Harris, REDISCOVERING FANON takes a poignant look at the parallels between modern oppression and past theories of anti-colonial philosopher Frantz Fanon, whose writings shaped the Black Panther Party and sparked a revolution of libertarian thinkers.

items.title: FREE JOAN LITTLE
items.body:
In Cinema – Maysles Documentary Center

TICKETS

General Admission: $15 / Reduced: $7

FREE JOAN LITTLE

Yoruba Richen, 36 minutes, 2025

FREE JOAN LITTLE tells the story of the 1975 groundbreaking case of Joan Little, who was the first woman in U.S. history to be acquitted for using deadly force to resist sexual assault. At 20 years old, Joan (pronounced Jo-Ann) Little was incarcerated in North Carolina when she killed a white jailer she said tried to rape her. Her trial drew international attention, becoming a rallying point for civil rights, women’s rights and prison reform. The case brought together activists, including Angela Davis and Rosa Parks, and catalyzed an international conversation about sexual assault and racial justice that has reverberations to this day. With rare archival footage, contemporary interviews and the folk anthem that carried her cause, Free Joan Little captures the spirit of resistance that made history. The film features Oscar-nominated actress Danielle Brooks (The Color Purple) as the voice of Joan.

TO BE FOLLOWED BY Black Panther Party shorts

MAD BILLS TO PAY

Joel Alfonso Vargas, 2025, 103 min

19-year-old Dominican American Rico (Juan Collado) figures he’ll ride out the summer selling his homemade “nutcracker” cocktails (rum, vodka, juice) on Orchard Beach and hanging out with his friends. But after his girlfriend, Destiny (Destiny Checo), moves into his family’s already-crowded apartment, the two must face a new, adult reality. Bronx-born debut filmmaker Vargas based MAD BILLS TO PAY on his own experiences, shot the film guerilla-style in 14 days, and cites influences as disparate as John Cassavetes, Pedro Costa, and Andrea Arnold.

items.title: 67 Bombs to ENID
items.body:
In Cinema – Maysles Documentary Center
Thursday, September 17th, 2026 at 7PM

TICKETS

General Admission: $15 / Reduced: $7

67 BOMBS TO ENID

Kevin Ford and Ty McMahan, 88 min

Between 1946 and 1958, the United States of America conducted 67 known nuclear weapons tests in the Marshall Islands, on Bikini and Enewetak Atolls. Decades later, thousands of Marshallese survivors and their descendants now live in the United States and one such community has settled on the plains of Enid, Oklahoma. 67 BOMBS TO ENID is an intimate, character-driven documentary that weaves first-hand accounts of the detonations with the testimony of the generation born after — tracing displacement, generational trauma, and a community’s insistence on joy and cultural pride in the unlikeliest of American towns. It speaks to the need for durable solutions to the harms caused by the nuclear legacy, as well as the Marshallese peoples continued pursuit of nuclear justice. Executive Produced by Errol Morris.

items.title: THE AGGRESSIVES
items.body:
In Cinema – Maysles Documentary Center

Sunday, September 13th, 2026 at 6:30PM

TICKETS

General Admission: $15 / Reduced: $7

THE AGGRESSIVES

Daniel Peddle, 2005, 75 min, DCP

Filmed over five years, starting in 1999, Daniel Peddle's THE AGGRESSIVES takes place in New York City and closely follows the experiences of six "aggressives," a term that refers to young, queer, masculine-presenting people of color. These experiences reflect the challenges of life on the margins, including but not limited to jail time, hard labor, child-rearing, military service, and more. Despite these difficulties and disapproval from society at large, they achieve joy, love, and success. 

 
 

There is a wide range of gender expression among the film's subjects; the aggressives are not a monolith. Marquise is a trans man who enlists in the military, Kisha is a fashion model who radically swings from masculine to feminine, while Flo is a masculine-presenting person who frequently judges at balls. THE AGGRESSIVES gives equal voice to all of these complex identities.

items.title: NATIVE SON
items.body:
In Cinema – Maysles Documentary Center

Sunday, September 13th, 2026 at 3PM

TICKETS

General Admission: $15 / Reduced: $7

NATIVE SON

Pierre Chenal, 1951, 104 min, DCP

Based on the 1940 novel of the same name by American author Richard Wright (who also stars in the film and co-wrote the screenplay with French director Pierre Chenal), NATIVE SON is a classical Argentine melodrama following Bigger Thomas, a young black man who takes a job as a chauffeur to a wealthy white family in Chicago. The plot thickens when Bigger accidentally commits a murder and tries to cover it up. An oft-overlooked link in the history of film noir, NATIVE SON fits the movement in terms of both visual style and content. Due to its “controversial” nature, the film was severely censored in the United States.

The Library of Congress later undertook a restoration of the film, with consultation by the Smithsonian Institution, which replaced about 30 minutes that had previously been cut. The fully restored film, stitched together by negatives from the Argentine 16mm print and an incomplete 35mm print stored in the Archivo General de Puerto Rico, premiered at the Museum of Modern Art in 2016. 

The film will be introduced by John Bohn. Writer, organizer, and graduate of the Center for the Study of Ethnicity and Race, a research center founded by student protest at Columbia University. His essay “Narrating Self-Abolition: On Richard Wright” was recently published in e-flux Journal. His writing has also appeared in Screen Slate, Jacobin, and Hard Crackers: Chronicles of Everyday Life.

BAM BAM: THE SISTER NANCY STORY

Alison Duke, June 2024, 98 min
Producers: Alison Duke, Ngardy Conteh George

The iconic track “Bam Bam” has left a mark on music since taking the industry by storm in 1982, but what do we know of the incredible artist who laid her passionate vocals down to give it life?

Sister Nancy is one of the most legendary Dancehall artists to grace a mic, and yet the understanding of her impact and legacy suffers beyond diehards of the genre. It’s time to rectifythat. The song that has become a sample darling and star-making vehicle for many artists now brings into focus the trials, tribulations and rousing success of its original songstress.

items.title: IN JACKSON HEIGHTS
items.body:
In Cinema – Maysles Documentary Center
Co-presented with UnionDocs / Wiseman's New York

Thursday, September 10th, 2026 at 7PM

TICKETS

General Admission: $15 / Reduced: $7

IN JACKSON HEIGHTS

Frederick Wiseman, 2015, 190 min., DCP

Widely recognized as one of the most significant documentaries of the 21st century so far, Frederick Wiseman's IN JACKSON HEIGHTS documents everyday activities in the Queens district, which claims to be the most diverse neighborhood in the world. Wiseman's 40th documentary follows a Muslim school, a Jewish center, a meeting of LGBTQ+ people, a City Council office, and the local headquarters of Make the Road New York. With the keen eye of an anthropologist, Wiseman immerses the audience in the sights and sounds of Jackson Heights without offering a narrative or precise interpretation. Without being steeped in ideology, IN JACKSON HEIGHTS expresses the idea that the people are what make a city truly great. 

Screening presented in partnership with UnionDocs, as part of their ten day Civic and Cinematic Survey, an immersive look into Wiseman's New York through film, conversation, and New York City itself. Led by film scholar and independent programmer Genevieve Yue.

items.title: LOVE, WOMEN AND FLOWERS
items.body:
In Cinema – Maysles Documentary Center

Thursday, September 3rd, 2026 at 7PM

TICKETS

General Admission: $15 / Reduced: $7

LOVE, WOMEN AND FLOWERS

Marta Rodriguez and Jorge Silva, 1988, 58 min., DCP

Join us for a special screening of LOVE, WOMEN AND FLOWERS, a powerful film that explores the hidden labor, politics, and environmental costs behind the beauty of flowers. The evening will feature an introduction by Claudia Horn, author of Rosa’s Herbarium, a book that illuminates Rosa Luxemburg’s relationship to the natural world and the political and poetic life of plants. Together, the film and book offer a rich meditation on flowers, beauty, labor, and liberation.

About the book:

Better known for her revolutionary politics, Rosa Luxemburg was also an avid botanist. Between 1913 and 1918, even while incarcerated in Poland and Germany for her anti-war organizing, Luxemburg collected plants sent to her by friends or found in the prison grounds. With care and expertise, she pressed and annotated close to four hundred varieties of leaves and flowers.

This lavishly illustrated study, the first of its kind, brings together pages from Luxemburg’s herbarium, personal letters that richly detail her fascination with nature, and a discussion of her ecological critique of colonial capitalism.

Through the lens of the herbarium, Claudia Horn illuminates the connections between the study of flora, the naturalist movement, and the plantation economy, showing that the decolonization of botany and global environmental justice are both possible and necessary.

About the Film:

No matter the time of year, carnations in every color are readily available for purchase in the United States. These flowers are beautiful, but what is the cost? In Colombia, 90,000 women workers are endangered by hazardous working conditions in the flower industry. LOVE, WOMEN AND FLOWERS documents these women's personal accounts and efforts to organize.

Restoration made possible by the support of the Ministry of Culture of Colombia, the production, supervision and management of Felipe Colmenares, and the cultural exchange with the National Film Library of Ecuador “Ulises Estrella.”

The screening will be followed by a book signing by Claudia Horn, author of Rosa Luxembourg's Herbarium: Radical Ecology and the Global Plantation. The filmmakers' daughter, Sara Silva, will be in attendance.

Post-screening discussion and book signing with Claudia Horn!
